newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson sees brighter mobile phone market - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson sees brighter mobile phone market - paper.

text.p: Swedish telecoms giant Ericsson said the short- and long-term prospects for the global mobile phone market are brighter than expected, according to an interview in a Swedish newspaper.
Claes Tadne, market analysis manager for Ericsson Radio Systems, said the company's forecasts for this year were on the low side.
"The global market is growing faster than we expected," Tadne told business daily Dagens Industri.

Ericsson's current forecast, which was presented early this spring, suggested that 129.5 million people worldwide would have subscriptions to a mobile phone network in 1996 and the number of subscribers would grow to 433 million by 2001.
Dagens Industri said this forecast was now too modest and several telecommunications analysts consulted by the paper forecast Ericsson would need to strongly revise its long-term forecast upwards.
Tadne said the market was growing faster than expected.
"This is primarily the case in Asia and the Pacific Rim region. There is phenomenal growth in Japan, Australia and China. But other markets are changing as well."
